Original Requirements: A patient monitoring program is required for the ICU in a hospital. Each patient is monitored by an analog device which measures factors such as pulse, temperature, blood pressure, and skin resistance. The program reads these factors on a periodic basis (specified for each patient) and stores the factors in a database. For each patient, safe ranges for each factor are also specified by medical staff. If a factor falls outside a patient's safe range, or if an analog device fails, the nurses' station is notified.
Product Goals: Ensure patient safety through real-time anomaly detection
Provide reliable data storage and retrieval for medical records
Minimize false alarms to reduce nurse fatigue
User Stories: As a nurse, I want to receive immediate alerts when a patient's vitals exceed safe ranges
As a doctor, I want to view historical trend data for a patient's vital signs
As a technician, I want to be notified if an analog device fails or disconnects
As a medical staff member, I want to configure safe ranges for each patient individually
As a system admin, I want to ensure data integrity and secure access to patient records

Requirement Analysis: The system requires real-time data ingestion from analog devices via periodic polling. It needs a robust database schema to store time-series vital data linked to patient profiles. A rule engine is necessary to compare incoming data against configurable safe ranges per patient. Alerting mechanisms must be immediate and distinct for vital anomalies versus hardware failures. Security is paramount due to patient data sensitivity. The system must handle concurrent monitoring for multiple patients without latency.
Requirement Pool: Implement real-time data ingestion from analog devices for pulse, temperature, BP, and skin resistance
Develop alerting system for out-of-range vitals and device failures notified to nurses' station
Create database schema to store patient profiles and historical vital sign data
Build interface for medical staff to configure individual safe ranges per patient
Implement data export functionality for management reports and analysis
UI Design draft: A dashboard-style interface for the nurses' station. Main screen shows a grid of patient cards, each displaying current vitals with color-coded status (Green=Normal, Red=Alert). Clicking a card opens a detailed view with historical graphs. A sidebar allows configuration of safe ranges. Alert pop-ups must be prominent but dismissible. Dark mode support for night shifts.
